title: Power Apps: Power Apps CLI commands to find connectors and create connections for code apps
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, connector commands, licensing alternatives and governance controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes documented enforcement when code apps launch from the unconfirmed effect of data policies on CLI connection creation.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Power Apps code apps > Enable code apps reaches the environment control.
claims.quote:
Go to Manage > Environments > select the environment where you use code apps.
Go to Settings > Expand the Product subsection > Select Features.
Go to the feature Power Apps code apps and use the Enable code apps toggle to turn it on.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Block blocks a blockable connector in an existing policy.
claims.quote:
Select the Prebuilt connectors step in the Edit Policy process.
For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Connectors <connector-objects> -Classification <General|Confidential|Blocked> changes connector classification in the specified DLP policy.
claims.quote: The Add-ConnectorsToPolicy takes the connectors as a list of objects and adds them to the specified group of the given DLP policy. If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group.

claims.claim: The allowed classifications General, Confidential and Blocked correspond to Non-business, Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: Each connector object passed to Add-ConnectorsToPolicy needs id, type and name properties.
claims.quote:
Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties:
- id: The unique identifier of the connector.
- type: The type of the connector:
- name: The friendly name of the connector

claims.claim: The documented tenant-level data policy procedures require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: The documented environment-level data policy procedures require Power Apps Environment Admin permissions when the environment has no Dataverse database.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: For environments with a Dataverse database, the environment-level data policy procedures require the System Administrator role instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Data policies control connector use and combinations within their environment scope, including code apps at launch.
claims.quote:
Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.
Connectors for sensitive data. Connectors in this group can't share data with connectors in other groups.

claims.claim: Learn does not assign individual preview or generally available phases to these new connector CLI commands.
claims.quote: Searched: "code apps" "CLI" "preview" "connector". Opened create-connection and CLI reference; neither assigns these commands phases. The Copilot plugin is labelled preview; the separate legacy pac code reference is preview, not a phase for pa connector commands.
